# Metric spec sheet (generated by analysis.py)

Every definition is a column of the named SQL file, computed from `sql/base_orders.sql`. Divergence is the largest monthly gap between two definitions as a percent of their mean, over 2017-03 to 2018-08.

| Metric | Definitions | Largest divergence | Recommended | Why | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GMV (`sql/metric_gmv.sql`) | **a**: item price plus freight, every order whatever its status<br>**b**: payments received at face value, every order<br>**c**: item price without freight, orders not cancelled or unavailable | 19.9 % (b vs c, 2017-03) | **a** | GMV is demand placed, so it takes every order at the value the customer agreed to. Payments carry voucher and rounding noise, and dropping freight changes the number by a sixth. | finance analytics |
| Delivered revenue net of cancellations (`sql/metric_delivered_revenue.sql`) | **a**: delivered orders, item value plus freight, by purchase month<br>**b**: delivered orders, item value plus freight, by delivery month<br>**c**: payments of every order not cancelled or unavailable, by purchase month | 43.4 % (b vs c, 2017-11) | **a** | Product and marketing compare months by when the order was placed, and the last two months are restated as deliveries complete. Finance keeps definition b for recognition, labelled as such. | finance analytics |
| On-time delivery rate (`sql/metric_on_time.sql`) | **a**: delivered orders received on or before the estimated day<br>**b**: delivered orders received before the estimated day's midnight<br>**c**: every live order, with orders never delivered counted as not on time | 4.6 % (a vs b, 2018-08) | **a** | The promise to the customer is a day, not a midnight. Orders still in transit belong in a separate backlog metric rather than in the denominator. | logistics |
| Average review score (`sql/metric_review_score.sql`) | **a**: every review row, by the month the review was created<br>**b**: latest review per order, by purchase month<br>**c**: latest review per delivered order, by purchase month | 7.0 % (a vs c, 2018-04) | **b** | One vote per order, attributed to the purchase month so it lines up with the other metrics. Undelivered orders are kept because their reviews are the complaint signal. | customer experience |
| Active customers (`sql/metric_active_customers.sql`) | **a**: distinct customer_unique_id with any order in the month<br>**b**: distinct customer_unique_id with a delivered order placed in the month<br>**c**: distinct customer_id, the per-order key | 6.7 % (b vs c, 2017-03) | **a** | customer_unique_id is the person. customer_id is issued per order and counts orders, which is the mistake the source invites. | growth |
| Repeat rate (`sql/metric_repeat_rate.sql`) | **a**: share of the month's orders placed by a customer with an earlier order<br>**b**: share of the month's customers with more than one order anywhere in the data<br>**c**: share of the month's first-time customers back within 90 days | 101.8 % (b vs c, 2017-12) | **c** | A fixed 90-day window gives every cohort the same chance to return, so months are comparable. Definition b changes every time the data are refreshed. Definition a stays as a monitoring series. | growth |

## The single table

`sql/base_orders.sql` holds one row per order with purchase month, status flags, item value, freight, payments, the latest review score and the customer's order number. Every recommended definition is a GROUP BY over that table, so the six metrics reconcile to the same order count.
